evidence: From the car park follow the rough farm road down to river level, then pick up the orange triangular markers and follow these across the open flats to the bush line and the start of the track.
Cross this and follow the benched track, dropping to the Hokitika riverbed some 600 m from the road end.
From the road end there is approximately 5 km of rough farm road to follow before the Hokitika Gorge Road is reached.
Alternatively access can be gained from the Whitcombe Valley Road (Hokitika Gorge Road) and the route walked in the reverse order to that described.

doubts: Start: the text says only to follow the road as far as the vehicle will allow, after turning off the Kokatahi/Lake Kaniere circuit road; no road-end feature clearly matches. F2 (where an unnamed track meets Middlebranch Road) is the only road end on the Toaroha side, but the text does not name Middlebranch Road, so the start ref is null. End: the Whitcombe-side road end has no matching feature, so null. F1 is where a track meets Cedar Flat Bridge, which the text says is crossed to the huts; it is used as a via, not as a road end. The 5 km rough farm road beyond the road end is recorded as an exit, since the way ends at the road end. The Toaroha River crossing is tagged as a ford from the text's wording that the crossing can become impassable, which implies unbridged; this is an inference. Rapid Creek is tagged as a ford from 'Once across Rapid Creek' and the note that the swing bridge was removed; it is an inference too. The route does not go over the true Toaroha Saddle, but over a low saddle to the west. The Hokitika Gorge Road to Hokitika is 30 km and not walked. Median and Esma Creeks are noted as hazards but not as named crossings on the way. Route can be walked in reverse from the Whitcombe Valley Road, which is not a separate way.
